referencePeriods.GDP: 1981–2024, with Northwest Territories and Nunavut from1999

calculation.baseline: Intercept and one lag of annual provincial real GDP log growth; refitted at each origin
calculation.comparisonSample: Every candidate and its baseline use the same annual observations and held-out origins within each jurisdiction and horizon.

models.label: WTI price change
models.features: Baseline plus contemporaneous annual WTI log change

models.label: Supply and demand shocks
models.features: Baseline plus annual sums of all four Baumeister–Hamilton posterior median structural shocks

models.label: OPEC supply news
models.features: Baseline plus annual sum of Känzig oil supply news shocks

calculation.errorUnit: percentage points of cumulative real GDP change
calculation.errorScreen: At least 12 held-out years and 10% lower mean absolute error than the no-oil baseline
limitations: Uses revised GDP and the latest available estimated shock vintages, not data available at historical release dates.
Oil prices and identified shocks in the held-out year are treated as observed inputs; these are conditional checks, not advance forecasts.
Annual aggregation does not identify the within-year timing of shocks. Shock-model identification and posterior uncertainty are not propagated.
No model coefficients are selected or tuned on the holdout scores. Error-screen thresholds are application release criteria, not claims from the cited papers.

publicForecastGate.reason: Historical episodes are available. A validated conversion from an arbitrary oil-price change to a provincial GDP forecast is not.
requirements: Identify the supply or demand intervention and validate its mapping to the chosen WTI price path.
Propagate shock-identification, parameter and future-outcome uncertainty.
Validate with historical data vintages and independent provincial review before enabling forecasts.

literature.title: Estimation and Inference of Impulse Responses by Local Projections
Not All Oil Price Shocks Are Alike
Structural Interpretation of Vector Autoregressions with Incomplete Identification
literature.authors: Christiane Baumeister and James D. Hamilton

literature.title: The Macroeconomic Effects of Oil Supply News

limitations: The observed GDP changes include every economic influence during those years; they are not effects caused only by oil.
Nominal US-dollar WTI changes are compared with real Canadian-dollar GDP growth. No exchange-rate or inflation-adjusted oil-price equivalence is implied.
GDP is expenditure-based at market prices, distinct from the basic-price energy GDP in the income view.
Northwest Territories and Nunavut histories begin in 1999. Earlier combined-territory figures are not reassigned to either jurisdiction.
Nearest episodes are chosen only by the annual oil-price change, not economic similarity or the sign of subsequent GDP.

reproduction.design: For each province and horizon0,1,2 regress cumulative GDP log change on lagged GDP growth and either oil log change, all four BH structural shocks, or Känzig supply-news shock. Fit ordinary least squares on common candidate years. At each heldout year from2006, only use training rows whose outcomeYear is earlier, with at least18training rows. Convert predicted log changes to cumulative percent before scoring. Never map selected arbitrary WTI percentages into these research estimates.

interpretation: A statistical error screen is not causal identification or public forecast approval. All126candidate projections remain research-only. Historical episode selection uses oil price distance alone; all observed GDP paths include other contemporaneous influences.
